St. Sebastian Dabovich

Saints

St. Sebastian Dabovich

St. Jovan Dabovich · St. Sebastian of Jackson

Period
1863–1940; glorified by the Serbian Orthodox Church in 2015
Region
United States, Alaska, Russia, Serbia, Japan
Titles / vocation
Venerable · Priest · Missionary
Commemoration
November 30

Introduction

St. Sebastian Dabovich is an American-born Orthodox missionary and writer of Serbian background. His travels and English publications belong to the history of a multiethnic North American mission, rather than only one immigrant community.

Read the published life [1]

Death / martyrdom

Reposed at Žića in 1940; no execution in the published life

Read circumstances and sources

Background

Born in San Francisco to Serbian emigrants, Jovan studies at Kiev and Saint Petersburg. He receives monastic tonsure and diaconal ordination in 1887 and returns to the United States, later serving as priest under Bishop Nicholas.

[1] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 1, 2

The Canadian historical biography expands the North American setting: church schools, teaching, worship, and journeys among scattered communities. It describes travel to the Pacific Northwest and Canada and the effort to organize congregations without a settled priest. Its date styles are not silently converted into a competing civil calendar.

[2] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Early missionary years, North American travels and teaching, before the Minneapolis section

Life and notable events

The OCA credits him with the first Serbian parish in America, at Jackson in 1894. Under Tikhon he works in mission administration and preaches in English, Serbian, and Russian. Later journeys take him repeatedly across the Atlantic and Pacific.

[1] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 2, 3, 4, 5

The Canadian account describes English portions at the dedication of Saint Sava’s church in Jackson and further work in Seattle, Wilkeson, Butte, and Alaska. It also follows the Serbian mission within the wider North American diocese. This places national pastoral care alongside cooperation under the missionary bishops.

[2] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Jackson dedication; Pacific Northwest, Butte and Alaska communities; establishment of Serbian mission

Death and martyrdom

He spends his final years at Žića and reposes in 1940. The OCA gives November 17/30, preserving both printed dates. His relics are returned to Jackson in 2007. No martyrdom by execution is reported.

[1] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 6

Writings and legacy

Dabovich’s own 1898 preface addresses Orthodox brethren and children in the English-speaking world. He offers lives of saints together with lectures and sermons for devotional family reading and school use. He says he wishes the recorded lives themselves to speak and identifies Scripture and the early Fathers as the foundation of his instruction. This is evidence of his publishing purpose in his own lifetime, distinct from a later canonization biography. The surviving scan also identifies him as compiler and translator and locates publication at the Murdock Press in San Francisco. Its dedication remembers Metropolitan Isidore’s support for the young North American Church. Broken words in the retained OCR are summarized rather than quietly repaired into an allegedly verbatim quotation.

[3] Public-domain historical edition · Original title page, dedication, and preface, San Francisco, 1898

The OCA records his glorification by the Serbian Church in 2015, with the formal celebration in California.

[1] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 7, 8

The Canadian account’s bibliography includes English books of preaching, saints’ lives, and explanations of services. It connects these publications with his missionary activity, showing that travel, liturgical work, and accessible English reading belonged to the same pastoral undertaking.

[2] Published ecclesiastical life or account · English-language publishing and closing assessment, with bibliography
